sentences.text: The genus name Astrophocaudia means 'non-twisting tail' because of the closely connected hyposphene-hypantrum articulation in the tail vertebrae.
The name can also mean 'star tail' since the tail vertebrae resemble a three-pointed star when viewed from behind.
This dinosaur is unique among sauropods due to the planar orientation of its tail vertebrae joints and specific laminae in front of the neural arches.
Some researchers estimated the animal was about 10.9 meters long and weighed 2.85 tonnes.
Other researchers estimated the animal could have been up to 18.3 meters long and weighed 20 tonnes.
The fossil remains of Astrophocaudia were discovered in the Paluxy Formation.
The specimens SMU 61732 and SMU 203/73655 were discovered and excavated by Robert Slaughter in the 1960s.
The species name slaughteri honors Robert Slaughter, who originally discovered the fossils.
Phylogenetic analysis places Astrophocaudia at the base of the Somphospondyli group, outside of Titanosauria.
This sauropod lived during the Albian stage of the Early Cretaceous in Texas, United States.
It lived approximately 112 million years ago during the Early Cretaceous in what is now North America.
